description: Part 2 (distributed tracing, ALTERNATIVE B): add service-b (a second instrumented FastAPI microservice, NOT Lambda), wire the api to call it over HTTP so a request flows Client->api->service-b producing a REAL distributed trace with parent-child spans via W3C traceparent propagation. Add the OTel Collector contrib 0.109 and Jaeger 1.60 all-in-one to docker-compose.yml and configure OTLP export, plus Grafana correlation (trace_id in logs -> Jaeger). DEPENDS ON FEAT-001 (extends its app/ and docker-compose.yml; app/otel.py and the api service already exist).
steps: Create service-b/ FastAPI service (service-b/main.py) with its own endpoints: GET /process (normal downstream work) and GET /slow-process (injects extra bounded latency to demonstrate a bottleneck). Serve on 0.0.0.0:8001.

service-b/otel.py: OTel SDK 1.27.0 TracerProvider, resource service.name=obs-lab-service-b, OTLP exporter to http://otel-collector:4317, FastAPI auto-instrumentation (0.48b0). Add a manual span only for a meaningful internal operation (not duplicating the auto FastAPI span).
service-b/requirements.txt (same pinned OTel/FastAPI/uvicorn set as app) and service-b/Dockerfile (python:3.12-slim, uvicorn on 8001).

Modify app/main.py: add an endpoint (e.g. GET /checkout) that makes an httpx GET to http://service-b:8001/process (and a variant hitting /slow-process to demonstrate latency). The already-configured httpx auto-instrumentation injects W3C traceparent so service-b continues the same trace. Do not add duplicate manual spans around the auto-instrumented httpx call.

config/otel/otel-collector-config.yml: receivers otlp (grpc 0.0.0.0:4317, http 0.0.0.0:4318); processors memory_limiter (reasonable check_interval + limit_mib), resource, batch; exporters otlp to jaeger:4317 with tls insecure; service.telemetry logs enabled; pipelines traces: [otlp receiver] -> [memory_limiter, resource, batch] -> [otlp exporter]. NO native jaeger exporter (removed in 0.109).

Update docker-compose.yml: add otel-collector (otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.109.*, mount config, internal-only 4317/4318) and jaeger (jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.60, env COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true, UI 16686 internal-only reached via SSH tunnel). Ensure api and service-b have OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317 and the OTel enable flag set. Confirm service-b target in prometheus.yml is now reachable.

Confirm Grafana correlation already provisioned in FEAT-001 works end to end: Loki derivedFields regex captures trace_id from the JSON logs and links to Jaeger; Jaeger tracesToLogsV2 links a span back to Loki. Adjust the regex/datasource uids if needed.
acceptance_criteria: `docker compose config` valid with otel-collector and jaeger added; both build/pull.
`docker compose up -d` brings api, service-b, otel-collector, and jaeger up healthy.
Hitting the api cross-service endpoint produces, in the Jaeger UI (via tunnel/port), a SINGLE trace_id containing parent-child spans from both obs-lab-api and obs-lab-service-b.
The /slow-process path shows the added latency as a longer span in that trace.
API JSON logs carry a non-empty trace_id for traced requests, and the Loki->Jaeger (and Jaeger->Loki) links resolve in Grafana.
verification: docker compose up -d && docker compose ps
curl -s http://localhost:8000/checkout >/dev/null; then open Jaeger UI and confirm one trace spans both services with parent-child spans
curl -s http://localhost:8000/checkout?slow=1 >/dev/null; confirm the service-b span shows the injected latency
In Grafana Explore (Loki) confirm trace_id derived field links to Jaeger and back
findings:
IMPLEMENTED & VERIFIED LIVE (local Docker Desktop 29.8.2 on macOS; committed on branch main).

=== WHAT WAS ADDED (Alternative B: second real microservice, NOT Lambda) ===
- service-b/: FastAPI downstream service on 0.0.0.0:8001. Endpoints GET /health, GET /process (bounded 0.05s work), GET /slow-process?seconds=<=5 (default 1.0s, demonstrates a bottleneck), GET /metrics (prometheus-client, so the pre-existing service-b scrape job is now UP). Package is copied to /srv/service_b in the image; CMD uvicorn service_b.main:app. __init__.py added so imports resolve inside the container.
- service-b/otel.py: OTel SDK 1.27.0 TracerProvider, resource service.name=obs-lab-service-b, OTLP gRPC exporter to http://otel-collector:4317, FastAPI auto-instrumentation (0.48b0). Gated by OTEL_ENABLED (no-op when off), mirroring app/otel.py. get_tracer() returns the configured tracer (or global no-op).
- service-b has exactly ONE manual span `service-b.work` (inside _do_work), representing meaningful internal work; the HTTP-handler span is the FastAPI auto span, so no duplication.
- app/main.py: new GET /checkout?slow=0|1 that makes an httpx AsyncClient GET to service-b (/process or /slow-process). NO manual span wraps the httpx call (httpx auto-instrumentation already creates the client span and injects W3C traceparent). Added SERVICE_B_URL env (default http://service-b:8001) and /checkout to the root endpoint list.
- config/otel/otel-collector-config.yml: receivers.otlp grpc 0.0.0.0:4317 + http 0.0.0.0:4318; processors memory_limiter(check_interval 1s, limit 256MiB, spike 64MiB), resource(upsert collector.name), batch(5s/512); exporters.otlp -> jaeger:4317 tls.insecure=true; service.telemetry.logs.level=info; pipeline traces: otlp -> [memory_limiter,resource,batch] -> otlp. NO native jaeger exporter (removed in contrib 0.109), as required.
- docker-compose.yml: added service-b (build ./service-b, image obs-lab-service-b:1.0.0, container obs-lab-service-b, internal-only 8001, OTEL env), otel-collector (otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.109.0, config mounted at /etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yml, internal-only, depends_on jaeger), jaeger (jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.60, COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true, UI 16686 internal-only). api gained SERVICE_B_URL + depends_on service-b. All on obsnet.
- Grafana correlation (Loki derivedFields <-> Jaeger tracesToLogsV2) was pre-provisioned in FEAT-001; confirmed correct, NO changes needed to datasources.yml.

=== REQUIRED FIX TO FEAT-001 ARTIFACTS (build-dependency bug, not a behavior/product change) ===
- OTel instrumentation 0.48b0 imports pkg_resources at runtime, but python:3.12-slim no longer bundles setuptools -> setup_otel() hit ImportError and silently disabled tracing (trace_id was ''). Added `setuptools==75.*` to BOTH app/requirements.txt and service-b/requirements.txt. After this, OTEL_ENABLED=true actually turns tracing on and trace_id is populated in logs. This latent bug only surfaced in Part 2 (Part 1 never enables OTEL). Needed to meet FEAT-002 acceptance; not a design decision.

=== VERIFICATION RESULTS (all run live) ===
- `docker compose config`: valid with otel-collector + jaeger.
- `docker compose build api service-b`: both images build (obs-lab-api:1.0.0, obs-lab-service-b:1.0.0).
- `OTEL_ENABLED=true docker compose up -d`: service-b, otel-collector, jaeger, and the Part-1 services all Up. (api host port 8000 was occupied by an unrelated process on this host -- same situation FEAT-001 noted -- so api was run internal-only via a throwaway `ports: !reset []` override; the committed compose keeps api on 8000, correct for EC2. All cross-service traffic is on the internal obsnet network and needs no host port.)
- GET /checkout -> ~72ms; GET /checkout?slow=1 -> ~1018ms (injected latency clearly visible).
- Jaeger /api/services lists obs-lab-api AND obs-lab-service-b. Fetching the slow trace by its id (taken from the api JSON log's trace_id) shows a SINGLE trace with correct parent-child spans across both services:
    obs-lab-api: GET /checkout (root, 1017.7ms)
      -> obs-lab-api: GET (httpx client span, 1009.2ms)
        -> obs-lab-service-b: GET /slow-process (1007.3ms; parent is the api span => W3C traceparent propagation confirmed)
          -> obs-lab-service-b: service-b.work (1004.3ms; the single manual span carrying the injected latency)
  So the ?slow path shows the added latency as a longer span, as required.
- API JSON logs carry a non-empty trace_id (e.g. e1d2043282786d3c09a606362bdd3f93) for traced /checkout requests.
- Prometheus active targets: api, node_exporter, prometheus, service-b all `up` (service-b now reachable via its new /metrics).
- Loki: the exact trace_id values present in Jaeger were found in {service="obs-lab-api"} logs, and the datasource derivedFields regex "trace_id\"\s*:\s*\"([a-f0-9]+)\" captures them -> the Loki->Jaeger link resolves to real traces (and Jaeger tracesToLogsV2 links back to Loki). Verified at the data level; the clickable Grafana UI link uses the pre-provisioned uids loki/jaeger.
- `pytest tests/`: 12 passed (no regressions from the /checkout + requirements changes).
- `docker compose down`: clean.

=== HANDOFF NOTES ===
- To get traces you MUST start the stack with OTEL_ENABLED=true (e.g. set it in .env). With OTEL_ENABLED=false the whole stack still runs and OTel is a no-op (Part 1 behavior preserved).
- No AWS resources were created; all verification was local Docker.
- Jaeger UI 16686 and collector 4317/4318 are internal-only (SSH tunnel on EC2), consistent with the lab's port policy.
